text:
kai: Started a canary on inference-api and seeing weird skew — config is 10% but logs show ~40% of some users hit the canary. Anyone seen this before?

sara: :eyes: Which routing policy did you pick in the rollout? header, hash, cookie?

kai: Using variant_split_v2 with user hashing (user_id) + cookie fallback. Also have an optional header guard `x-canary-flag`.

ben: Any chance cookie scope/path is involved? We had a similar case where path mismatch caused double-matching.

kai: Posting the rollout snippet I used:
```yaml
split:
  - variant: canary
    pct: 10
    guard:
      header: "x-canary-flag"
  - variant: stable
    pct: 90
```

maria: Telemetry shows three different assignment flows: header->cookie->hash, but the runtime patch last week changed priority to header->hash->cookie in some codepaths. Could be related.

deploy-bot: Canary started for service inference-api @kai (10%)

kai: I repro'd in staging: users with an old `session_variant` cookie set at path `/dashboard` sometimes end up routed by hash, sometimes by header. It looks like cookie path normalization is stripping `/dashboard` -> `/` and then the cookie influences hashing for unrelated routes.

ben: Can you paste a minimal log for a single request?

kai: Sure:
```
[2026-03-12T14:21:02Z] routing: incoming headers: x-canary-flag=, cookie=session_variant=canary; cookie_path=/dashboard
[2026-03-12T14:21:02Z] routing: normalized cookie_path=/ -> hashed_user=0x7f -> bucket=0.42 -> assigned=canary
[2026-03-12T14:21:02Z] routing: header check: x-canary-flag= (empty) -> continuing
```

sara: Ah — normalization in runtime v0.23.1 stripped cookie path for storage. That means legacy cookies scoped to `/dashboard` are now normalized to `/` before hashing. Previously we ignored path for hashing.

maria: Telemetry cohort for `legacy-cookie` shows bucket drift of +18% during the canary timeframe. This matches the 10%->40% symptom.

ben: So potential fixes: (A) revert normalization, (B) include cookie_path as salt in hash, or (C) add an explicit guard to ignore cookies unless path matches route prefix. Which is lowest risk?

kai: Reverting normalization is risky since it touches storage semantics. I can open a small hotfix to include `cookie_path` in the hash salt so the same cookie won't affect routes outside its path.

deploy-bot: Canary scaled to 0% by @kai

telemetry-bot: Alert: bucket drift > 15% for inference-api canary at 2026-03-12T14:25:30Z

sara: Also filing a console UX item: show `cookie_scope`/`path` in the rollout editor and a tooltip about legacy cookies. Product owners keep assuming cookies are route-scoped.

maria: Filed as PROJECT-1123: "Expose cookie scope in rollouts and warn about legacy cookie behavior". Adding telemetry tag `legacy-cookie` to the alert.

ben: Kai — ping me when PR is up. We should also add an e2e that simulates cookies with various paths to prevent regression.

kai: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/inference/pulls/4512 — changes: add cookie_path to hash salt + unit tests + telemetry tag for legacy-cookie cohort. Will deploy to staging after CI.

maria: :thumbsup: Also please add a small migration note for support so they can explain to customers.

ben: Nice. Follow-up: consider making header guards higher priority in the rollout UI, or at least clearly document priority ordering. This caused confusion.

kai: Agree. I'll add changelog + console note. Rolling back the canary bought us time. Thanks everyone for quick triage.
